body:
Why State police remain central

Under the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, police and public order are State subjects. Consequently, Gujarat Police has the primary responsibility for detecting and investigating cybercrimes that fall within its jurisdiction. National institutions may provide technical support and coordination, especially where an incident involves several States or financial institutions.

Gujarat Police maintains specialised cybercrime arrangements, including the State Cyber Crime Cell under CID Crime and related cybercrime support and capacity-building facilities. The State's Cyber Centre of Excellence is part of this broader effort to strengthen cybercrime response.

A specialised cybercrime unit does not mean that every cybercrime is investigated only by that unit. Police stations and other authorised investigating agencies may perform functions according to their jurisdiction and assigned responsibilities.

What digital forensics means

Digital forensics is the scientific examination and interpretation of electronic information for investigative or evidentiary purposes. Its purpose is to help establish relevant facts through reliable examination of digital material.

Electronic evidence may be found in computers, mobile devices, storage media, electronic messages, photographs, video recordings and other digital records. A forensic examination may help determine what information is present, whether relevant records can be interpreted and how particular digital material relates to an investigation.

The examination must preserve the reliability of the evidence. This requires appropriate documentation, authorised handling and a clear record of custody. A chain of custody is the documented history of who handled an item of evidence and when. It helps a court assess whether the evidence can be trusted.

The Directorate of Forensic Science, Gujarat

Gujarat's Directorate of Forensic Science (DFS) functions under the State Home Department. Its Computer Forensic Division supports the scientific examination of electronic material, including digital devices and video evidence.

The DFS may provide findings and expert opinions that assist police investigations and judicial proceedings. The forensic laboratory does not itself replace the police investigator, public prosecutor or judge.

The National Forensic Sciences University

National Forensic Sciences University (NFSU) is a central university and Institution of National Importance established under the National Forensic Sciences University Act, 2020. Its Gandhinagar campus has academic and training programmes in forensic science, cybersecurity and digital forensics.

NFSU contributes to specialised education, research and professional capacity building. It must be distinguished from the Gujarat DFS, which performs governmental forensic services, and from Gujarat Police, which carries out law-enforcement functions.

Police investigation, expert examination and judicial decision

In a cybercrime case, police may investigate the reported incident and collect relevant material through lawful procedures. A forensic laboratory may examine electronic evidence and provide an expert report. A prosecutor presents the case before the court, while the defence may challenge the evidence. The court considers the evidence and applicable law before deciding the case.

An electronic record or forensic report does not automatically prove that a particular person committed a crime. Its relevance, reliability and legal significance must be assessed in the proceedings.

Examining electronic evidence under the IT Act

Section 79A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 empowers the Central Government to notify specified departments, bodies or agencies of the Central Government or a State Government as Examiners of Electronic Evidence for providing expert opinions on electronic evidence before a court or other authority. This is a legal mechanism for expert examination, not a transfer of all police powers to forensic laboratories.

Prelims focus

  • Police and public order are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule.
  • Gujarat Police has specialised cybercrime arrangements under CID Crime.
  • Gujarat DFS functions under the State Home Department.
  • Digital forensics concerns scientific examination of electronic evidence.
  • NFSU was established under the National Forensic Sciences University Act, 2020.
  • Section 79A of the IT Act concerns Examiners of Electronic Evidence.
  • Trap: A forensic laboratory assists the justice process but does not decide criminal guilt.

[Sources: Gujarat Police, Gujarat Cyber Crime website, Initiatives of Gujarat Police Cyber Crime Cell, consulted 16 November 2026; Directorate of Forensic Science, Government of Gujarat, Computer Forensic Division, page updated 1 August 2026; National Forensic Sciences University, Gandhinagar Campus and Centre of Excellence pages, consulted 16 November 2026; Information Technology Act, 2000, section 79A, India Code; NCERT, Social and Political Life III, Class 8, Chapter 6, Understanding Our Criminal Justice System, printed pp. 74–75; Ministry of Home Affairs, National Cyber Crime Data, 21 July 2026.]

pictures.caption: Digital forensic laboratories help investigators examine electronic evidence scientifically.

pictures.alt: Police investigate, forensic specialists examine, prosecutors present and courts decide; NFSU is separate, and Section 79A provides for notified electronic evidence examiners.

title: Gujarat's Cybercrime Investigation and Digital Forensic Capacity

body:
Why different cybersecurity institutions exist

Cybercrime investigation, cybersecurity incident response and protection of essential infrastructure are related but different public functions. A fraudulent banking call requires a criminal-law response. A significant technical incident affecting an organisation may require cybersecurity assistance. A threat to essential infrastructure may demand attention to the continuity and safety of public services.

India therefore uses different institutions and legal provisions rather than assigning every cybersecurity function to a single organisation.

Important national and Gujarat institutions

InstitutionMain functionPrimary context
I4CCoordinates action against cybercrime.Complaints, police coordination and financial fraud.
CERT-InNational agency for cybersecurity incident response.Cyber incidents, alerts, advisories and response coordination.
NCIIPCNational nodal agency for Critical Information Infrastructure protection.Protection of computer resources essential to national security, economy, public health or safety.
Gujarat GSOCMonitors and strengthens cybersecurity for Gujarat government information infrastructure.State government systems and associated critical information infrastructure.
Gujarat PoliceInvestigates cybercrime under applicable law.Criminal complaints and offences within its jurisdiction.

CERT-In stands for Indian Computer Emergency Response Team. It is the national agency for activities such as collecting information on cyber incidents, issuing alerts and coordinating incident response.

NCIIPC stands for National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre. Its primary concern is the protection of information infrastructure whose failure could have serious national consequences.

I4C stands for Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre. It is concerned with strengthening the coordinated response to cybercrime, not with replacing every State police investigation.

Gujarat Security Operations Center

The Gujarat Security Operations Center (GSOC) operates under the Directorate of ICT and e-Governance within Gujarat's Department of Science and Technology. According to the State department, GSOC was established in May 2022.

Its responsibilities include monitoring cybersecurity issues affecting State government information infrastructure and coordinating with relevant agencies such as CERT-In and NCIIPC. It is especially associated with the security of important government systems hosted at the Gujarat State Data Center.

GSOC and Gujarat Police have different primary responsibilities. GSOC focuses on monitoring and protecting State government digital infrastructure. Police investigate criminal offences. The same incident may require cooperation between them.

Critical Information Infrastructure and protected systems

Section 70 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 defines Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) as a computer resource whose incapacitation or destruction would have a debilitating impact on national security, the economy, public health or safety.

Under section 70, the appropriate government may notify a computer resource directly or indirectly affecting CII as a protected system. The legal status arises through notification; it is not assigned merely because an organisation is large, important or profitable.

A large factory can be economically important without every computer in that factory being a notified protected system. Conversely, a computer resource supporting an essential service can be critical because of the consequences of its failure.

Important sections of the IT Act, 2000

SectionSubjectCore distinction
66CIdentity theftDishonest or fraudulent use of another person's specified digital identity features.
66DCheating by personationCheating through impersonation using a computer resource or communication device.
70Protected systemsGovernment notification of computer resources affecting CII.
70ANational nodal agencyStatutory basis for national CII protection arrangements.
70BCyber incident responseStatutory basis for CERT-In.
79AElectronic evidenceProvision for notified Examiners of Electronic Evidence.

Section 70A and section 70B are especially easy to confuse. Section 70A concerns the national nodal agency for CII protection. Section 70B concerns the national agency for cybersecurity incident response.

Prelims focus

  • Section 70: protected systems and the definition of CII.
  • Section 70A: national nodal agency for CII protection.
  • Section 70B: CERT-In and cybersecurity incident response.
  • Section 79A: Examiners of Electronic Evidence.
  • Gujarat GSOC was established in May 2022, according to the State Department of Science and Technology.
  • Trap: I4C, CERT-In, NCIIPC and GSOC do not perform the same principal function.

[Sources: Information Technology Act, 2000, sections 66C, 66D, 70, 70A, 70B and 79A, India Code; Information Technology (National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre and Manner of Performing Functions and Duties) Rules, 2013; CERT-In, Directions under section 70B, dated 28 April 2022, introductory provisions; Gujarat Department of Science and Technology, Projects and Initiatives, Gujarat Security Operations Center, consulted 16 November 2026; Ministry of Home Affairs, National Cyber Crime Data, 21 July 2026.]

pictures.alt: I4C coordinates cybercrime, Gujarat Police investigates, CERT-In responds to incidents, NCIIPC protects CII, and Gujarat GSOC monitors State infrastructure security.
pictures.caption: Cybercrime coordination, incident response and infrastructure protection serve different purposes.

title: Cybersecurity Institutions and the Information Technology Act: Who Does What?

body:
Why Gujarat's ports matter

Gujarat's position on India's western coast makes maritime trade an important part of its economy. Ports connect overseas shipping with Indian producers, consumers, industrial areas and transport networks. They handle goods that may include containers, petroleum products, chemicals, raw materials and manufactured products.

A port's hinterland is the inland area served by that port through transport and economic connections. Factories and markets in the hinterland depend on the movement of goods through the port. The port, in turn, depends on road, rail, communication, electricity and other supporting services.

Major and non-major ports in Gujarat

Indian port administration distinguishes major ports from non-major ports. This is a legal and administrative classification, not simply a ranking by cargo volume or commercial importance.

Deendayal Port, formerly Kandla Port, is Gujarat's major port. The Gujarat Maritime Board (GMB) is the State statutory body responsible for the administration and development of non-major ports within its jurisdiction.

Important Gujarat non-major port locations include Mundra, Pipavav, Hazira and Dahej. Some of these ports involve private development or operation. Private participation does not automatically change a non-major port into a major port.

Dated port classification: The Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways reported 1 major port and 48 non-major ports in Gujarat in its publication Update on the Indian Ports Sector, covering April–September 2025 and issued on 9 April 2026. These figures describe that reporting period; later notifications or administrative changes may alter the count.

Digital information in port operations

Modern ports use electronic records and communication to coordinate activities. Different systems may support vessel information, cargo documentation, terminal operations, gate movements, billing and links with transport operators. Because several organisations exchange information, the accuracy and availability of digital records matter.

For example, an incorrect shipment record may create a mismatch between goods and documents. An unavailable terminal information service may delay coordination. Exposure of commercially sensitive records may compromise confidentiality. These consequences are different, even when they arise within the same port environment.

Where IT and OT appear

  • IT functions: Cargo records, billing, commercial communication, administrative data and electronic documentation.
  • OT-related functions: Digital monitoring or control associated with physical equipment and terminal operations where such systems are installed.

Not every port system controls equipment. Likewise, a problem in an administrative database does not prove that cranes, gates or other physical equipment have been affected.

Why disruption may spread beyond the port

Port activity is connected with ships, terminal facilities, inland transport and industries receiving or supplying cargo. A prolonged interruption in one part of this network can delay another part. For instance, disrupted shipment coordination may delay the movement of an industrial raw material, even though the factory's own computer systems remain unaffected.

The correct security objective therefore depends on the function being protected: confidentiality of commercial records, integrity of cargo and movement information, and availability of services needed for trade.

Prelims focus

  • Deendayal Port is the major port in Gujarat and was formerly known as Kandla Port.
  • Gujarat Maritime Board is associated with the State's non-major ports.
  • Mundra, Pipavav, Hazira and Dahej are important non-major port locations.
  • The hinterland is the inland area economically served by a port.
  • A port's digital functions include information handling and, in some cases, monitoring or control of physical operations.
  • Trap: Major port and non-major port are administrative categories; private operation or high cargo volume does not by itself determine the category.

[Sources: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Update on the Indian Ports Sector, April–September 2025, issued 9 April 2026, section 2.2.1, Gujarat; Gujarat Maritime Board, GMB Owned Ports, consulted 16 November 2026; Government of Gujarat, Ports and Marine Sector in Gujarat, sections on Mundra, Pipavav, Dahej and Hazira, consulted 16 November 2026; NCERT, India: People and Economy, Class 12, Chapter 11, International Trade, printed pp. 125–131, especially Sea Ports as Gateways of International Trade.]
